body.answer:
A credit balance refund is issued for Title IV financial aid overpayments of $1.00 or greater. Credit balances from non-Title IV financial aid are subject to a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check, mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up at Student Accounts. [1]

3. Click Electronic Refunds under My Profile Setup.
4. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if already completed): under Security Settings, select a passcode method (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode, and click Verify.
5. Under Payment Profile, edit an existing payment method or create a new one. Check the box in Refund Option to designate it as the direct deposit refund account.

For a withdrawal refund, deadline and refund percentage depend on the course/session. Student Accounts has the current refund-period deadlines. [3][10]

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [30]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

A student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline. The academic calendar lists the deadline for each course session [14]. After the refund period has ended but before the deadline, you may withdraw online through Web Self Service; the course withdrawal form can also be accessed online or completed in the Office of the Registrar. Once processed, the course receives a “W” on your transcript, with no refund. Instructor permission is not required. If you have a registration hold, use the Withdrawal Form or email reg@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo account with your name, Ramapo ID (R#), CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title. After withdrawing from all courses, complete the WD/LOA process in Connect [10][14].

For an extraordinary circumstance that prevented you from withdrawing on time, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal. Submit an appeal letter in your own words, supported by official documentation, to the Office of the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular (fall or spring) semester following the term. Explain the extraordinary circumstances, why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures or request/receive incompletes, and the term you want withdrawn. Typically, approved appeals result in W grades for all courses in that term [15].

Withdrawing can affect financial aid eligibility and satisfactory progress toward graduation [10]. If you drop below full-time status, aid may be adjusted; federal aid requires enrollment in 6 credits, and Pell, state aid, institutional grants, and scholarships may be reduced or canceled depending on your situation [3]. Financial Aid recommends meeting with its office to discuss the impact on your aid package [1]. For aid SAP, students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits; SAP is reviewed annually after spring. The policy also requires a 2.0 cumulative GPA for undergraduates and 3.0 for graduate students [2]. I don’t have verified information about how withdrawing from one particular class would affect your individual aid or SAP; Financial Aid can advise.

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
Apply online through the [Parking Permits registration portal](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/opr/OPRMain.aspx?IsAuth=1&groupid=102&groupname=PUBLIC+SAFETY). All student vehicles parked on campus need a valid permit. [7][11][24]

Before applying, ensure the parking fee has been applied to your student account. [7] Commuters receive a rearview mirror hangtag; you may register two vehicles on one permit at no additional fee, but only one registered vehicle may be on campus at a time. [1][7] Fees are charged to your student account, and off-campus students are also charged 6.63% NJ sales tax. [1][25]

As a new student, pick up your permit during New Student Check-In. [1][7] Park in the commuter B1, B2, or B3 lots. If your assigned lot is full, students may use C1, C2, or D lots as overflow. Commuters may not leave a vehicle parked overnight (2am–6am) without prior Public Safety authorization. [7][12]

For help, contact Public Safety.

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [29]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [29]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/parking/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/parking/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [30]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)

- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

A student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline. For extraordinary circumstances beyond your control, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal. Submit an appeal letter in your own words, supported by official documentation, to the Office of the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular semester following the term. Explain the circumstances that prevented completion and why you could not use standard withdrawal procedures or obtain incompletes; indicate the term you seek to withdraw from. Typically, an approved request results in W grades in all courses for that term. [11][14]

Withdrawing from a course may affect financial aid eligibility and satisfactory progress toward graduation. [10] If you officially withdraw or leave school before 60% of a semester concludes, federal regulations determine how much Title IV aid you may retain and how much must be returned. If you drop below full-time, aid may be adjusted; federal aid requires 6 credits in a semester, and state aid, institutional grants, and scholarships could be reduced or canceled. [1][3]

For financial-aid SAP, students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits; withdrawals count as attempted credits toward the 150% maximum timeframe. [2] For a late administrative withdrawal, contact the Office of the Provost. For aid and SAP questions, contact Financial Aid.

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [32]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

For a full-semester course, the withdrawal deadline was November 6, 2026, so it has passed. For a Session II course, the deadline is November 24, 2026, so you may still withdraw by then. [32]

A withdrawal completed by the published deadline results in a “W” on your transcript; there is no refund. You may not withdraw after the published deadline. Typically, approved appeals result in W grades in all courses for the term. [8]

The Registrar says instructor permission is not required, but encourages discussing the withdrawal with your professor. You can withdraw online through Web Self Service; students with registration holds can use the Withdrawal Form or email reg@ramapo.edu from their Ramapo email with their name, Ramapo ID number, CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title.
